questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence ****has an error and select ****the appropriate option. If ****a sentence is free from error, select ****‘No Error’.** 

Turning left under (1)/ the crossroads will (2)/ save you some time. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the sentence we find that:

The error is in part 1 of the sentence.

One cannot go under the crossroads, as it is not a bridge. Instead, it is a point where one reaches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

When we are referring to locations or points we should use the preposition at

Therefore the correct form will be: **At the crossroads**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

At a crossroads

At a point when a choice must be made; at a point of change.

 
• *After earning my degree, I'm at a crossroads. I need to figure out which direction my life should take.*
 
• *As a company, we're at a crossroads. We can continue business as usual, or we can take a risk and try to grow.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.** 

Implicit in the Satyagraha was Gandhi’s assumption that (1)/ all rulers are dependent on their position and power (2)/ upon the obedience and cooperation of the ruled (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that: 

 
• **In the second part of the sentence,** **'on'** is incorrect Instead use **'for'**
 
• **'For'** is a preposition and one of the meanings of it is** 'having as a purpose or function'** 
 
• Hence, this meaning is correct in the sentence.

**So the correct sentence is:**

*Implicit in the Satyagraha was Gandhi's assumption that all rulers are **dependent for** their position and power upon the obedience and cooperation of the ruled.*

questions.question:
**In the following ****question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate ****word. Select ****the ****correct alternative out of the four and indicate it ****by selecting the appropriate option. ** 

______European was seen eating Kadi Chawal in New Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **A**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Reading the sentence we find that: 

__
 
• Article **A **should be filled in the blank. 
 
• Thus the sentence will be "**A **European...."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Article **A **is used before words beginning with a **consonant **or with **a consonant sound. **
 
• In the given question the word European starts with a consonant sound i.e a 'Y' sound. 
 
• Therefore we should use **A **instead of **An**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• Seeing that the word European starts with a vowel one might think that '**an' **should be used. 
 
• But even though the word starts with a vowel the starting sound is that of a consonant. 

Therefore the correct answer is '**A European**.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word. ** 

Baroque
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Plain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the given word and the correct answer. 
 
• **Baroque**: A style used to create exuberance, grandeur and detail. 
 
 
• For Example - Their repertoire mixes **Baroque **works with contemporary music.
 
 
 
• **Plain**: Not decorated or elaborate; simple or basic.
 
 
• For Example - Their website is fairly **plain**, but very easy to navigate.
 
 
 
• Thus from the given points, we find that both the words express the opposite meaning. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Plain**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the **meanings **of the other given words. 
 
• **Decorative**: Serving to make something look more attractive. 
 
 
• For Example - He gave the picture a **decorative **border, which changed the look of the page.
 
 
 
• **Bizarre**: Very strange or unusual. 
 
 
• For Example - I had a really **bizarre **dream last night.
 
 
 
• **Rich**: Having a great deal of money or assets; wealth.
 
 
• For Example - He is determined to get **rich **quickly.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". ** 

I wouldn’t (has dared) to venture into such a scene.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **have dared**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that: 

 
• The sentence starts with **I **and therefore it should be followed by **have.**
 
• The tone of the given sentence indicates that it is in the past tense. 
 
• Therefore we should use **dared** instead of **dare**. 
 
• Using dare makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. As it is not the correct verb to fit the tense. 
 
• Thus from the given points, we can conclude that the correct answer is **have dared**. 

Correct Sentence: I wouldn't have dared to venture into such a scene.
